ordered_diagnoses: Bile duct stricture due to metastatic disease

finalists.label: Chemotherapy-induced sclerosing cholangitis
finalists.why: It has the most specific evidence, including marked elevation of liver enzymes and wall thickening of the extrahepatic and intrahepatic bile ducts.

finalists.label: Cholangitis
finalists.why: It has a broad range of evidence, including marked elevation of liver enzymes and wall thickening of the extrahepatic and intrahepatic bile ducts, with no evidence against it.

frontier_selector.why: The champion is chosen because it specifically accounts for the chemotherapy treatment and the resulting sclerosing cholangitis, which is a known side effect of certain chemotherapy agents.

support_spans: marked elevation of liver enzymes: AST 173 U/L, ALT 221 U/L, γ-GTP 2553 U/L, and ALP 5188 U/L
Abdominal ultrasonography showed wall thickening of the extrahepatic and intrahepatic bile ducts and of the gallbladder, with bile-duct strictures and dilatations
Contrast-enhanced CT confirmed wall thickening of both extrahepatic and intrahepatic bile ducts with luminal narrowing and dilation, and gallbladder wall thickening
cholangiography via the drainage tube revealed strictures and dilatations with irregular wall contours in the intrahepatic bile ducts of both lobes
contradict_spans: Biopsy of the common bile duct showed no malignant cells and only modest infiltration of neutrophils
